Read a NanoDrop One spectral export

Source: R/read_nanodrop.R
read_nanodrop.Rd

Parses a UV-Vis spectral .tsv file exported by a NanoDrop One into a long table with one row per sample measurement and wavelength.

Usage

read_nanodrop(
  filepath,
  min_wv = NULL,
  max_wv = NULL,
  remeasure_suffix = NULL,
  error
)

Arguments

filepath

Path to the exported .tsv file.

min_wv, max_wv

Optional numeric wavelength bounds (inclusive). NULL (the default) keeps the full measured range.

remeasure_suffix

Optional suffix that marks a re-measurement, e.g. "e". When set, a sample named "A" followed by one named "Ae" is treated as a replacement: the "A" measurements are dropped and "Ae" is renamed to "A". Names ending in the suffix with no matching original (e.g. "Rinse" with no "Rins") are left alone. NULL (the default) disables this.

error

Deprecated; use remeasure_suffix.

Value

A data.table::data.table() with columns:

samps

Sample name (character).

waves

Wavelength in nm (numeric).

abs

Absorbance (numeric).

measurement

Position of the measurement block in the file (integer).

timestamp

Timestamp line as written by the instrument (character).

Details

An export consists of one block per measurement: a sample name line, a timestamp line, a Wavelength (nm) header line, optional // calibration lines, and then tab-separated wavelength/absorbance pairs. Blocks are located by their header line, so the parser does not depend on the date format or locale of the instrument.

Every block becomes its own measurement, so measuring the same sample name twice yields two measurements rather than silently merging them.

See also

read_nanodrop_dir() to read every export in a folder.

Examples

path <- system.file("extdata", "nanodrop_example.tsv", package = "nanodRop")
spectra <- read_nanodrop(path)
head(spectra)
#>     samps waves    abs measurement         timestamp
#>    <char> <num>  <num>       <int>            <char>
#> 1:    6 1 190.0 10.666           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM
#> 2:    6 1 190.5 10.782           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM
#> 3:    6 1 191.0 10.853           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM
#> 4:    6 1 191.5 10.877           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM
#> 5:    6 1 192.0 10.866           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM
#> 6:    6 1 192.5 11.105           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM

# Restrict to the visible range
visible <- read_nanodrop(path, min_wv = 400, max_wv = 700)
